tex_content.html:
$M$ is obtained from components of $M'$ by connected sums, with possibly a finite number of additional connected sums with $S^1\times S^2$ and $\R P^3$.
Proof

↗ lem:kl-three-dimensional-solutions-existence-kappa-solutions-5 \sketch Components of $M-X$ are $\epsilon $-tubes or $\epsilon $-caps. A tube whose boundary spheres lie in distinct components of $X$ gives a connected sum of those components; a tube attached to one component gives an $S^1\times S^2$ summand. A $3$-ball cap has no effect, while an $(\R P^3-B^3)$ cap gives an $\R P^3$ summand.

□
